chunks: Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Sa'igh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Ghadrani narrated to us. He said: Abu Ali al-Husayn b. al-Layth b. Bahlul al-Mosuli narrated to us. He said: Ghassan b. al-Rabi narrated to us. He said: Sulaym b. Abdullah, the freedman of Amer al-Sha'bi, narrated to us from Amer, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said:
The affair of my Umma will continue to prevail until twelve caliphs have passed, all of whom are from Quraysh.

key_terms.أُمَّتِي: my Umma — the Muslim community as a whole
key_terms.خَلِيفَةً: caliphs — successors to the Prophet in leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.ظَاهِرًا: prevailing/dominant — the affair of the Umma remaining strong and victorious

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the twelve caliphs and the prevailing of his Umma?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s) states that the affairs of his community will remain dominant and victorious as long as twelve caliphs from Quraysh are in authority. This hadith is a parallel narration to the previous one (50:8) through a different chain of transmission via Amer al-Sha'bi, reinforcing the Twelve Successors tradition. Both Sunni and Shia scholars accept the historicity of this prophecy, though they differ on its referents.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Sa’igh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Ghadrani narrated to us. He said: Abu `Ali al-Husayn b. al-Layth b. Bahlul al-Mosuli narrated to us. He said: Ghassan b. al-Rabi` narrated to us. He said: Sulaym b. `Abdullah the slave of `Amer al-Sha`bi narrated to us from `Amer that he said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
The affair of my Umma will continue to prevail until twelve caliphs have passed – all of whom are from Quraysh.
